noodles/2cbee41:
The load-time randomizer was rolling the mix itself: bass presets
spanned 12.1 dB RMS (sub -4.2, deep -16.3), melody 10.1, harmony 5.3 —
some reloads slammed and some fell over, which is the opposite of a
magic scene. scripts/calibrate.mjs (npm run calibrate) renders every
preset through the real graph against a fixed reference scene and
prints the table; the gain trims here come from that measurement,
anchored to each track's median so the overall balance stays put.

Preset trims now live in a per-track Gain after the input compressor.
Pre-comp gain rides the drive distortion and the compressor knee, both
self-leveling, so trims there never converged (an 8 dB cut moved sub
by 0.7 dB). Drive keeps shaping tone at a fixed source level; the trim
does level, linearly.

Also measured, not guessed: bass octave-1 velocity boosts are now per
preset against the octave-2 gap (deep drops its boost entirely — a
louder 33 Hz sine only booms woofers, phone speakers stay deaf), and
magic-scene melody loses octave 2 (~4 dB down through its own 180 Hz
highpass, on top of sitting in the bass register).

After: harmony 0.9 / bass 0.6 / melody 1.7 / kits 0.6 dB spreads, and
six kit+preset master combos land within 0.6 dB of each other.
